# Colten Ellis

**Colten Ellis** (born October 5, 2000) is a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender for the Buffalo Sabres of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was selected in the third round, 93rd overall, by the St. Louis Blues in the 2019 NHL Entry Draft.

Prior to his professional career, Ellis played major junior hockey in the Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). During his tenure in the QMJHL, he established league records for the most career shutouts and the lowest goals-against average in a single season. In 2021, he was awarded the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy as the league's best goaltender.

Ellis made his NHL debut with the Buffalo Sabres in October 2025, becoming the first goaltender from Cape Breton Island to play in the NHL.

## Early life

Ellis was born on October 5, 2000, in River Denys, Nova Scotia, a small community on Cape Breton Island . He is the son of Brian and Jo-Ann Ellis and has one brother, Matt . He began playing organized hockey with the Whycocomagh Minor Hockey Association .

During his youth career, Ellis played for the Cape Breton West Islanders in the Nova Scotia U18 Major Hockey League. In 2017, he goaltended the team to the Telus Cup, Canada's national under-18 club championship. The Islanders became the first team from Atlantic Canada to win the tournament . In the championship game, Ellis made 43 saves and stopped a breakaway in overtime to secure the victory .

## Playing career

### Junior
Ellis was originally drafted by the Cape Breton Screaming Eagles in the fourth round (59th overall) of the 2016 QMJHL Entry Draft . He appeared in three games for Cape Breton during the 2016–17 season as a call-up while playing U18 hockey . In June 2017, the Screaming Eagles traded Ellis to the Rimouski Océanic in exchange for a first-round draft pick .

In his rookie season with Rimouski (2017–18), Ellis recorded 33 wins and 6 shutouts . He was named to the QMJHL All-Rookie Team and the Second All-Star Team . He was also awarded the Raymond Lagacé Trophy as the league's defensive rookie of the year . Following his second season with Rimouski, Ellis was selected by the St. Louis Blues in the third round of the 2019 NHL Entry Draft .

In June 2020, Rimouski traded Ellis to the Charlottetown Islanders in exchange for a third-round pick in 2020 and first- and second-round picks in 2021 . During the 2020–21 season, Ellis recorded a 23–1–0 record . He set a new QMJHL single-season record with a 1.78 goals-against average (GAA) and an .926 save percentage . On March 21, 2021, Ellis recorded his 18th career shutout in a 4–0 win against the Cape Breton Eagles, breaking the all-time QMJHL record for career shutouts previously held by Philippe Cadorette .

Following the 2020–21 season, Ellis was named to the QMJHL First All-Star Team and received the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy, awarded annually to the goaltender with the best goals-against average in the league .

### Professional
#### St. Louis Blues organization (2021–2025)
On March 1, 2021, Ellis signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the St. Louis Blues . He began his professional career during the 2021–22 season, splitting time between the Blues' affiliates, the Springfield Thunderbirds of the American Hockey League (AHL) and the Worcester Railers of the ECHL . He made his professional debut with Worcester on October 23, 2021, making 42 saves in a win against the Maine Mariners .

Ellis spent the majority of the 2022–23 season with the Tulsa Oilers in the ECHL, where he struggled with consistency and injuries, recording a 3.46 GAA and an .888 save percentage in 27 games . He later described this period as a time when he had to "relearn his love for hockey" .

In the 2023–24 season, Ellis played for the Orlando Solar Bears (ECHL) and the Springfield Thunderbirds (AHL). He was named the ECHL Goaltender of the Month for December 2023 . He eventually earned a larger role in Springfield, posting a .924 save percentage in 16 AHL games that season .

During the 2024–25 season, Ellis served as a primary goaltender for the Springfield Thunderbirds. He recorded a 22–14–3 record with a 2.63 GAA and a .922 save percentage, which ranked fourth in the AHL .

#### Buffalo Sabres (2025–present)
On October 5, 2025, the St. Louis Blues placed Ellis on waivers for the purpose of assigning him to the AHL . The following day, October 6, 2025, he was claimed by the Buffalo Sabres . The acquisition came as Buffalo dealt with injuries to goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and performance issues with other goaltenders on the roster .

Ellis made his NHL debut on October 22, 2025, starting in a home game against the Detroit Red Wings . He made 27 saves on 29 shots to secure a 4–2 victory . With this start, Ellis became the first goaltender from Cape Breton Island to play in the NHL . He was named the game's first star .

On December 9, 2025, during a game against the Edmonton Oilers, Ellis sustained a concussion following a collision with Oilers forward David Tomasek in the first period . He was removed from the game by concussion spotters and placed on injured reserve on December 11, 2025 . At the time of his injury, Ellis held a 4–3–0 record with the Sabres .

## International play

Ellis represented Canada White at the 2016 World Under-17 Hockey Challenge. In 2018, he was a member of the Canadian team at the IIHF World U18 Championships in Russia .

In December 2024, Ellis was named to Team Canada's roster for the Spengler Cup in Davos, Switzerland . He served as the starting goaltender, helping Canada advance to the semifinals. He finished the tournament with a 2.68 GAA and a .911 save percentage, the second-best statistical performance among goaltenders in the tournament .

Cape Breton goaltender beats small town odds, signs NHL contract
================================================================

20-year-old becomes first Cape Breton born goaltender to sign with an NHL franchise

Mar. 23, 2021 | 3:08 p.m.

By [Brad Chandler](https://signalhfx.ca/author/bchandler/)

3 min read

![Image 2](https://signalhfx.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/chandler-main.jpg)

caption Recent NHL signee Colten Ellis stands next to his hometown sign of River Denys, in March 2020, while wearing his St. Louis Blues draft jersey.

Brad Chandler

A Cape Breton goaltender defied the odds of small town hockey players earlier this month when he became the first island-born goalie to sign a National Hockey League contract.

River Denys’ Colten Ellis, 20, put pen to paper on March 1 to agree to a three-year entry-level contract with the St. Louis Blues.

According to Nova Scotia Sports Hall of Fame CEO Bruce Rainnie, this marked the first time in recorded history that a Cape Breton born goaltender has been offered an NHL contract.

“It doesn’t even feel real to be honest,” Ellis said in a recent interview. “Obviously playing in the NHL is something that I grew up dreaming of but coming from a small community it was something that seemed so far out of reach. For it to become a reality is pretty hard to put into words.”

Growing up in River Denys, a community of only 60 residents, Ellis faced various obstacles when trying to make it to the big leagues.

Beginning when he was 10, Ellis would rely on his family members to help improve his skills in between the pipes. He’d often spend his free time doing drills or training at the local rink.

Ellis, who is the starting goaltender for the Charlottetown Islanders of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL), spent countless hours travelling to camps and training sessions while growing up in hopes of improving his game.

Colten’s father, Brian Ellis, said in a 2020 interview that things were “really, really hard” for his son. “Where we live there’s basically nothing for goaltenders, so we did everything we could to help him get better,” Ellis said.

Brian Macinnis, president of Ellis’ midget team the Cape Breton West Major Midget Islanders, said that traveling is a hurdle many young Cape Breton hockey players face when trying to reach the next level in their hockey careers.

“For Colten, I really don’t think the travelling was something that affected him, he was firmly set on the goal he wanted to accomplish, and he didn’t let anything get in his way,” Macinnis said in an interview.

Hometown Support
----------------

Ellis, who is in his fourth and final year in the QMJHL, said having the opportunity to be signed by an NHL franchise is evidence that his hard work has paid off.

“Some people would ask me ‘where do you find your motivation from?’ being from a small community,” Ellis said. “I love to play hockey, so it was easy to wake up early and work out or go to a training session, I always had the motivation just from the support I had down home.”

Residents of River Denys and surrounding areas have followed Ellis’ journey over the past number of years, showing waves of support for their hometown boy by making social media posts, buying his jerseys, and attending his games. Locals say Ellis has gained somewhat of a celebrity status across the island.

“I don’t think people from home realize how much the support I get from them plays a factor in my motivation,” Ellis said. “There are so many people at home who send messages and send their support in their own way and it’s incredible to see. It makes me want to keep going and do it for everyone back home.”

Ellis’ contract will begin at the start of the 2021-2022 NHL season next October. He currently sits atop the QMJHL goalie rankings with a 16-1-0 record as well as a 1.89 goals against average and a .922 save percentage.

Colten Ellis is another new-era goaltender who mixes good buttefly style with great athleticism, strong technique, and excellent puck-tracking skills.

He burst onto scouts’ radar last year with his succes and accolades gathered with the Rimouski Oceanic. Any teams keeping an eye on the potential 2020 first overall pick, Alexis Lafrenière, would have seen how Ellis played.

Birthplace: **Whycocomagh, Nova Scotia, Canada**  
Catches: **Left**  
Position: **Goaltender**  
Height: **6’1”**  
Weight: **183 lbs.**  
Team: **Rimouski Oceanic (QMJHL)**

The trade that sent him from the Cape Breton Screaming Eagles to the Oceanic changed his projection. He truly found his footing with Rimouski and was able to make an impact. Last year, he played 51 games, ending the campaign with a 2.35 goal-against average and a .913 save percentage. He also posted six shutouts along the way and was named to QMJHL All-Rookie Team.

The first year with his new team gave him a future as professional goalie, The 2018-19 season helped him secure an NHL selection, perhaps in the first half of this year’s draft.

_In the video below, Ellis is #92 white jersey (G)_

Ellis isn’t the biggest goalie out there, but he isn’t small by any means. At 6’1”, he understands how to use his size to cover and cut angles.

His biggest strength seems to lie in his reaction time and agility. He’s a quick and shifty goaltender who’s able to follow the play and anticipate where he has to be in order to make the save. He is quick thinking, with good reaction time, and great awareness, and that makes him a tough goaltender to beat. He still has to polish a few aspects of his play if he wants to be able to dominate in the pro ranks, but there’s plenty of time to work on refinements.

As seen in the video, his puck-handling skills aren’t the most developed. He does an okay job passing to his teammates, but that’s the extent of the ability. He’s quick but could really limit the unneccesary movements he does when moving from one post to the other. He is also a bit of a risk-taker in some occasions, playing very aggressively at the edge of his crease. He also tends to really get absorbed in the play, sometimes to his disadvantage.

Still, due to his fairly good skill set, he’s able to make the save more often than not. Such habits could be toned down with time, especially if he learns to maximize his aggressive stance with a sound technical foundation.

It was recently confirmed that Ellis has received an invitation to participate in Team Canada’s camp to evaluate players for the 2020 World Juniors, to be held June 5-8. Scouts and management do seem to believe Ellis has potential and could be good enough to carry Canada to a medal next year.

His potential is undeniable. He is still a bit raw in a few respects, but will continue to develop with time.

### Rankings (not all rankings are final)

Future Considerations: **#56**  
McKenzie/TSN: **#51**  
NHL Central Scouting: **#8** (NA Goalies)

For a team in need of goaltending depth, Colten Ellis is a fair bet to take late in the second round or early in the third. He has the makings of a potential starter, with the usual mix of athleticism, good hockey sense, and strong technical build. As long as the team selecting him doesn’t have any pressing need right now, the decision could pay off in a few years’ time.

Colten Ellis has quickly become a part of the Charlottetown Islanders’ organization
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By Jason Malloy, PNI Atlantic

Last updated Mar 17, 2025

![Image 2: Goalie Colten Ellis tracks a shot during Tuesday’s Charlottetown Islanders’ practice at MacLauchlan Arena.](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/colten-ellis-has-quickly-become-a-part-of-the-charlottetown-islanders-_qyu2djw.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&h=216&sig=cekZ6K3jYlO9CB9yB7tdIA)

Goalie Colten Ellis tracks a shot during Tuesday’s Charlottetown Islanders’ practice at MacLauchlan Arena. Photo by Jason Malloy /Jason Malloy

CHARLOTTETOWN, P.E.I. — Colten Ellis has made a seamless transition to his new team.

The River Denys, N.S., native has fit right in with the Charlottetown Islanders after spending the first three years of his junior career with the Rimouski Oceanic. The Isles acquired the overage goalie in a blockbuster deal during the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League draft on June 6.

“It’s been great,” Ellis said before Tuesday’s practice. “The biggest thing was everyone here was really welcoming to me and helped make that transition as easy as possible. Everybody has been very supportive.”

![Image 3: Colten Ellis flashes the leather in making a glove save during Tuesday's Charlottetown Islanders' practice at MacLauchlan Arena. - Jason Malloy](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/dsc2435_pdonbd7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=M5dNlaE03wE6qWTn7iJ6JQ)

Colten Ellis flashes the leather in making a glove save during Tuesday’s Charlottetown Islanders’ practice at MacLauchlan Arena. – Jason Malloy

Islanders’ veteran Thomas Casey said he has been texting back and forth with Ellis since the trade.

“When we met (on Day 1 of camp) it was like we’ve known each other for a while,” he said. “He’s a good Cape Breton guy, so it was very easy to make conversation with him.”

Jim Hulton, the Isles’ head coach and general manager, said Ellis’ professionalism is what has stood out most to him.

“I think that’s the word that jumps out when I think about him,” he said of the St. Louis Blues’ third-round draft pick, who won the Telus Cup in 2017 with the Cape Breton West Islanders.

“He has a quiet, calm demeanour – which I think is great for a goaltender,” Hulton said, noting Ellis moves quick in the crease and has really good rebound control.

#### Need to know

Who: Colten Ellis, the Charlottetown Islanders’ No. 1 goalie.  
Acquired: The Islanders traded a third-round pick in 2020, plus their own first- and second-round picks in 2021 to Rimouski for Ellis at the draft in June.  
Personal: Ellis turns 20 on Oct. 5. He is a six-foot-one, 182-pound goalie from River Denys in Cape Breton, N.S.  
Ellis said: “Being a lot closer to home and being with a great organization like this, it’s going to be pretty awesome.”  
The mask: Ellis recently received his new Islanders’ mask for the season. The Confederation Bridge is prominently displayed on the right side while the swing bridge at the Canso Causeway, connecting Cape Breton to mainland Nova Scotia, is on the left. A big Islanders logo adorns the top while his number – 92 – is on the chin.

Ellis, who turns 20 on Oct. 5, was acquired to help bridge the gap from veteran Matthew Welsh to Jacob Goobie, who is entering his sophomore year in Charlottetown, as the Islanders’ No. 1 goalie. Team officials put an emphasis on addressing the role heading into the off-season.

“When a guy like Colten comes on the market, you have to do what it takes to get him here,” Hulton said.

He added the market for such goalies is traditionally limited, and the prices increase during the Christmas trade period.

“And that’s a bold statement because we paid a lot, but honestly we thought the price was going to be even higher at Christmas.”

![Image 4: Colten Ellis, right, speaks with Charlottetown Islanders' goalie coach Paul Drew prior to Tuesday's practice. - Jason Malloy](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/dsc2305_xkvrbqi.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=mucaA68_ujWLFQKOFQxjXg)

Colten Ellis, right, speaks with Charlottetown Islanders’ goalie coach Paul Drew prior to Tuesday’s practice. – Jason Malloy

Ellis and Goobie already had a good working relationship before camp as the duo trained together the past two summers with Scott Gouthro in Cape Breton. The relationship has been fostered by goalie coach Paul Drew in Charlottetown.

“He’s been really helpful,” Goobie said of Ellis. “He’s been giving me little tips as I go along. He’s a really easy guy to talk to and has just been awesome to everybody in the room as well.”

Ellis sees it as a two-way street.

“He’s, obvious, going to be an awesome goalie in this league. I am going to learn from him and he’s going to learn from me, too, so it’s a win-win for both of us.”

Goobie is a competitor and wants to push for as many games as he can but is also thankful for the opportunity to be able to grow alongside veterans like Welsh and Ellis.

“I definitely can’t complain, that’s for sure, (they are) two amazing guys to learn from.”

![Image 5: Charlottetown Islanders' goalie Colten Ellis stops defenceman Lukas Cormier during practice Tuesday at UPEI. - Jason Malloy](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/dsc2431_sry6mp5.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=Vy_181dimyP4U0HKrsH_YA)

Charlottetown Islanders’ goalie Colten Ellis stops defenceman Lukas Cormier during practice Tuesday at UPEI. – Jason Malloy

The trade brings Ellis back to the Maritimes to complete his junior career. During his tenure with the Oceanic, Rimouski would visit each of the Maritime teams once during the season. This year, he will only play in the Maritimes due to the coronavirus (COVID-19 strain) pandemic.

“I will get to see my family and friends a lot more, so it’s exciting.”

But it also may mean he won’t get to play another game in Rimouski, Que., unless the teams meet in the playoffs, for which a format has yet to be announced.

“Rimouski is always going to hold a special place in my heart,” Ellis said. “Right from Day 1 they were so good to me and welcoming. My billet there, (Marie Soucy), was an unbelievable person. She really made me feel at home, going into a French city … and not knowing any French at all.”

Ellis and Summerside native Carson MacKinnon lived with the same billet family for two years before MacKinnon was traded to the Gatineau Olympiques. MacKinnon is attending UPEI this year and playing for the Panthers, so the two have been able to spend some time together.

Ellis has only played half a game during the pre-season but can see the regular season is nearing.

“It’s been a long time coming,” Ellis said.

“We have a great group of guys and going into the season it’s pretty exciting,” he added. “I think we’re going to be able to do a lot of damage here.”

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

| Playing career | 2021–present |

**Colten Ellis** (born October 5, 2000) is a Canadian professional [ice hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey "Ice hockey") player who is a [goaltender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goaltender "Goaltender") for the [Buffalo Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Sabres "Buffalo Sabres") of the [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hockey_League "National Hockey League") (NHL). He was selected 93rd overall by the [St. Louis Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Blues "St. Louis Blues") in the third round of the [2019 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NHL_entry_draft "2019 NHL entry draft").

Born and raised in [River Denys, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Denys,_Nova_Scotia "River Denys, Nova Scotia"), Ellis emerged as one of Atlantic Canada's top young goaltenders while playing for the Cape Breton West Islanders, leading the team and province to its first-ever [Telus Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telus_Cup "Telus Cup") in 2017. Following his performances with the Islanders, he went on to play major junior hockey in the [Quebec Major Junior Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_Major_Junior_Hockey_League "Quebec Major Junior Hockey League") (QMJHL) with the [Cape Breton Screaming Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Screaming_Eagles "Cape Breton Screaming Eagles"), the [Rimouski Océanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimouski_Oc%C3%A9anic "Rimouski Océanic"), and the [Charlottetown Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlottetown_Islanders "Charlottetown Islanders"). During his time in the QMJHL, Ellis made a name for himself, earning defensive rookie of the year and a spot on the all-rookie team his first year. Described as an athletic goalie before the 2019 NHL entry draft, he was selected by the St. Louis Blues with the 93rd overall pick. In his final QMJHL season, he tied the career QMJHL shutout record, broke the best goals-against-average season record, and had the fourth-best season save percentage all time. He was also named the best goaltender of the year and earned a spot on the first all-star team.

After signing an entry-level contract with St. Louis in 2021, Ellis spent several seasons developing within the organization. He began his professional career with the [ECHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECHL "ECHL")'s [Worcester Railers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_Railers "Worcester Railers") before earning opportunities with the [American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League") (AHL) [Springfield Thunderbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield_Thunderbirds "Springfield Thunderbirds"). Following subpar performance marked by inconsistent play and a mid-season injury that sidelined him for the rest of the 2022–23 season with the ECHL [Tulsa Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Oilers "Tulsa Oilers"), Ellis rebounded after relearning his love for hockey. In the following seasons, his statistics and play improved, eventually earning the Thunderbirds' starting role. In October 2025, the Blues placed Ellis on waivers, where he was claimed by the Buffalo Sabres. He made his NHL debut later that month, becoming the first goaltender from [Cape Breton Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Island "Cape Breton Island") to play in the NHL. Internationally, he has represented the [Canada national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_men%27s_national_ice_hockey_team "Canada men's national ice hockey team").

Ellis was born in [River Denys, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Denys,_Nova_Scotia "River Denys, Nova Scotia") on October 5, 2000, to Jo-Ann and Brian Ellis as one of three children in the family.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) He began playing hockey with the [Whycocomagh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whycocomagh "Whycocomagh") Minor Hockey Association,[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Whycocomagh-3) and had trouble throughout his childhood finding consistent playing time and competition, which his father helped him out with.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-4) Ellis has one brother, Matt, and one cousin, Chase, who played in the QMJHL with him.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Rimouski-5)

Ellis joined the Nova Junior X-Men of the Nova Scotia Under-15 Major Hockey League in the 2013–14 season as his first step into amateur hockey and stayed for 2014–15, having a 2.08 [goals against average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goals_against_average "Goals against average") (GAA) and a 1.61 GAA respectively.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Following the two seasons with the X-Men, he joined the Cape Breton West Islanders of the Nova Scotia Under-18 Major Hockey League for the 2015–16 season, putting up a .890 save percentage and a 3.70 GAA.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)

Following his performance with the Islanders, the [Cape Breton Screaming Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Screaming_Eagles "Cape Breton Screaming Eagles") selected Ellis in the fourth round of the 2016 [Quebec Major Junior Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_Major_Junior_Hockey_League "Quebec Major Junior Hockey League") (QMJHL) entry draft with the 59th overall pick. This was considered a noticeable drop from his expected draft position, with Screaming Eagles scouts surprised that he was still available to pick in the fourth round.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-trade-6) He attended the Screaming Eagles training camp but was assigned back to the Islanders.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Rimouski-5) Ellis brought the Islanders to winning the provincial championship, and they were entered into the Atlantic Region [Telus Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telus_Cup "Telus Cup") qualifier. They beat out the Moncton Flyers to earn themselves a spot in the Telus Cup, where they went on to become the first Nova Scotia team to win the Telus Cup.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-SO-7) Ellis performed exceptionally well in the finals and overall, with 43 saves and an overtime breakaway in the final game, along with having a 2.20 GAA and a .929 save percentage in the tournament.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Whycocomagh-3) Ellis was also called up to the Screaming Eagles throughout the [2016–17 QMJHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_QMJHL_season "2016–17 QMJHL season"), playing three games with a 2–0–0 record, a 2.50 GAA, and an .885 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-trade-6) After the end of the 2016–17 season, the Screaming Eagles decided to trade one of their three goaltenders, putting them all on the trade block. On June 3, 2017, Ellis was traded to the [Rimouski Océanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimouski_Oc%C3%A9anic "Rimouski Océanic") for a first-round pick in the 2018 QMJHL entry draft, opting to keep their goaltenders Kyle Jessiman and [Kevin Mandolese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Mandolese "Kevin Mandolese").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-trade-6)

Ellis began the [2017–18 QMJHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_QMJHL_season "2017–18 QMJHL season") in Rimouski along with goaltender Jimmy Lemay. At the time, Rimouski general manager and head coach Serge Beausoleil did not decide on who would be starting in net for the season, as he wanted to watch and see how they develop in net.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-8) Ellis quickly took over the starting role, playing 51 games and leading the Océanic to the QMJHL playoffs. In the QMJHL playoffs, they faced the [Moncton Wildcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncton_Wildcats "Moncton Wildcats") in the first round, which they lost in seven games.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) He ended his rookie season in the QMJHL first in wins with 33 and in shutouts with 6. He was also third in goals against average and save percentage, with 2.35 GAA and .913%, respectively.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-9) He was nominated for the [RDS Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RDS_Cup "RDS Cup"); the QMJHL rookie of the year, and the [Raymond Lagacé Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Lagac%C3%A9_Trophy "Raymond Lagacé Trophy"); the defensive rookie of the year. Teammate [Alexis Lafrenière](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Lafreni%C3%A8re "Alexis Lafrenière") won the RDS Cup while Ellis won the Raymond Lagacé Trophy. He was also named to the All-Rookie team and the second All-Star team.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Rimouski-5)

Rimouski continued to have Ellis as the starting goaltender beginning the [2018–19 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_QMJHL_season "2018–19 QMJHL season"). Ellis was one of 40 players selected for the 2019 [CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CHL/NHL_Top_Prospects_Game "CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game"), intended as a showcase for the 2019 eligible draftees.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-10) He played just under 30 minutes in net, saving 15 out of 17 shots on goal.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-11) By the end of the season, Ellis was ranked eighth across all North American goaltenders for the [2019 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NHL_entry_draft "2019 NHL entry draft").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-12) In 46 games, he would record a 2.47 GAA and a .910 save percentage. Rimouski entered the 2019 playoffs as the third seed in the eastern conference, beating out the [Chicoutimi Saguenéens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicoutimi_Saguen%C3%A9ens "Chicoutimi Saguenéens") and the Screaming Eagles before being swept by the [Rouyn-Noranda Huskies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rouyn-Noranda_Huskies "Rouyn-Noranda Huskies") in the semi-finals; Ellis had played 12 games with a 2.36 GAA and .919 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Among the media during draft talk, he was described as a very "athletic goalie" but was "moving too much" and "not tracking pucks as well as he could."[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-13) The [St. Louis Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Blues "St. Louis Blues") selected Ellis in the third round with the 93rd overall pick in the 2019 NHL entry draft.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-14)

Ellis was returned to Rimouski for the [2019–20 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_QMJHL_season "2019–20 QMJHL season") after being drafted.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-15) He played in September and October before sustaining an injury that required surgery, which prevented him from playing in November and December.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-16) At the time of his injury, he had played 14 games with a 2.61 GAA and a .905 save percentage.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-17) On March 12, the QMJHL season was suspended for a week due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") and was [cancelled for the rest of the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_ice_hockey "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on ice hockey") on March 18.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-18) Ellis had played 29 games with a 2.41 GAA and a .904 save percentage when the season ended.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Following the end of the 2019–20 season, the [Charlottetown Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlottetown_Islanders "Charlottetown Islanders") traded for Ellis, giving up a 2020 third-round pick, and a 2021 first- and second-round pick.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-19)

Despite the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic causing the 2020–21 season for the [Ontario Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario_Hockey_League "Ontario Hockey League") to be cancelled and the [Western Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hockey_League "Western Hockey League") to start delayed, the [2020–21 QMJHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_QMJHL_season "2020–21 QMJHL season") continued as normal. Ellis started the season with a spot on the Week 3 QMJHL Team of the Week on October 19, recording a shutout against the [Halifax Mooseheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_Mooseheads "Halifax Mooseheads").[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-20) On March 1, 2021, Ellis signed his three-year, entry-level contract with the Blues, beginning in the [2021–22 NHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NHL_season "2021–22 NHL season").[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-21) On March 22, Ellis set the all-time QMJHL record for shutouts by a goaltender with eighteen by shutting out his former team, the Screaming Eagles, 4–0.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-SO-7) He was also named Player of the Week the same day, after recording two shutouts that week.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-22) By the end of the season, he had seven shutouts, tying the single-season shutout record at the time with seven, held by six goalies, including [Hockey Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockey_Hall_of_Fame "Hockey Hall of Fame") inductee [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo").[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) With a record of 23–1–0 with a 1.78 GAA and .926 save percentage, Ellis set the lowest GAA for a season by a goaltender in the QMJHL, and the fourth-best all-time save percentage. For his performance in the regular season, he received the [Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Plante_Memorial_Trophy "Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy") for best goaltender and a spot on the First All-Star team.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-2021Awards-24) Ellis led the Islanders to the semi-finals of the playoffs against the [Victoriaville Tigres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoriaville_Tigres "Victoriaville Tigres"), where they lost the series 2–3.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-25)

By the [2021–22 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_ECHL_season "2021–22 ECHL season"), Ellis had aged out of the QMJHL and began his professional career, participating in the Blues' preseason training camp. After what was described as a "strong showing", he was assigned to the [Worcester Railers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_Railers "Worcester Railers") in the [ECHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECHL "ECHL").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-26) He made his professional debut on October 23 against the [Maine Mariners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Mariners_/(ECHL/) "Maine Mariners (ECHL)") in a 4–3 win, saving 42 out of 45 shots on goal.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-27) A week later on October 30, he was called up to the [American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League") (AHL) [Springfield Thunderbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield_Thunderbirds "Springfield Thunderbirds").[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-28) He made his AHL debut against the [Bridgeport Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport_Islanders "Bridgeport Islanders"), saving 28 out of 29 shots on goal in a 4–1 win.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-29) He was sent down the next day back to the Railers. On December 9, Ellis was called up again to the Thunderbirds, staying with them for almost two months.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-30) He was sent down to the Railers for the final time on January 22.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-31) In six games on the season with the Thunderbirds, he had recorded a 1–3–2 record, a 3.93 GAA, and a .880 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) On March 18, Ellis recorded his first professional shutout against the [South Carolina Stingrays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Stingrays "South Carolina Stingrays") in a 3–0 win, making 23 saves.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-32) By the end of the season, he played 34 games with the Railers with a 15–13–5 record, a 3.21 GAA, and a .905 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)

Entering the [2022–23 ECHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_ECHL_season "2022–23 ECHL season"), Ellis participated in the Blues' Traverse City prospect tournament. He did not perform well, giving up nine goals in two starts, being pulled early both times.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-33) Ellis, along with [Joel Hofer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Hofer "Joel Hofer") and Vadim Zherenko, made the Thunderbirds opening roster.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-34) Despite being on the season-opening roster, Ellis never played a game and was assigned to the ECHL [Tulsa Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Oilers "Tulsa Oilers") on October 29.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-35) Ellis took over the Oilers starting goaltender following his reassignment. With the Oilers, he started suffering issues with his hip beginning in December and had season-ending hip surgery in February. At the time of surgery, he had finished the season with a 12–9–5 record, 3.46 GAA, and an .888 save percentage in 27 games.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-PNI-36) Ellis began his recovery period and was back on the ice in June. While recovering from his injury, Ellis had relearned his love of hockey and "re-modelled \[his\] game and took a look at what \[he\] needed to do to have some success".[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-PNI-36)

Prior to the [2023–24 ECHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_ECHL_season "2023–24 ECHL season"), Ellis participated in the Blues' training camp, where he suffered a concussion.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) He ended up being assigned to the [Orlando Solar Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Solar_Bears "Orlando Solar Bears") to start the season. Following an impressive performance with a record of 5–0–0 with one shutout, a 1.58 GAA, and a .954 save percentage, Ellis was named ECHL Goaltender of the Month for December. He was also named ECHL Goaltender of the Week ending December 23 with 2 wins, a 1.00 GAA, and a .973 save percentage.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-37) After Thunderbirds goalie Vadim Zherenko suffered an injury in January, Ellis was called up to the Thunderbirds on the 21st, playing 13 games and recording a 2.86 GAA and a .926 save percentage while Zherenko was out. Following Zherenko's return from injury, the Thunderbirds rotated him, Zherenko, and [Malcolm Subban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Subban "Malcolm Subban") in net before Subban was traded in March to the [Columbus Blue Jackets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus_Blue_Jackets "Columbus Blue Jackets").[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) Following the trade, Zherenko and Ellis became the Thunderbirds goaltender tandem and were in net for the rest of the season, playing three more games for a season total 2.89 GAA and .924 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Ellis credited Subban for his better performance in Springfield throughout the year.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) On June 11, Ellis signed a one-year, two-way contract extension worth $775,000 with the Blues.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-38)

Ellis started the 2024–25 season by participating again in the Blues' training camp, where he would be assigned to the Thunderbirds to start the season.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-39) Despite Zherenko starting in the Thunderbirds net on opening night, he quickly took over as the team's starting goaltender, playing 8 out of the 12 games from the start of the season to mid-November with a .919 save percentage and a 2.80 GAA between that time period.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-40) Following his strong start to the AHL season, he continued to be the Thunderbirds' starting goaltender. On March 6, Ellis signed a two-year, two-way contract extension worth $1.55 million with the Blues.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-41) Four days later, he was named AHL Player of the Week ending March 9 with a shutout, 95 saves, a 0.72 GAA, and a .979 save percentage.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-42) By the end of the season, he had played 42 games with a 22–14–5 record, a 2.63 GAA, and a .922 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) The Thunderbirds entered the [2025 Calder Cup playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Calder_Cup_playoffs "2025 Calder Cup playoffs") as the A6 seed paired against the A3 seed [Providence Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_Bruins "Providence Bruins"), a series they would lose in three; he recorded a 2.32 GAA and a .933 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Following the Calder Cup playoffs, Ellis was called up to the Blues on April 28, but did not appear in any Stanley Cup playoff games.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-43)

Before the start of the [2025–26 NHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_NHL_season "2025–26 NHL season") on October 5, the Blues put Ellis on waivers to be put on assignment back to Springfield as [Jordan Binnington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Binnington "Jordan Binnington") and [Joel Hofer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Hofer "Joel Hofer") were expected to be the starter and backup, respectively.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-44) After impressive preseason play which caught the attention of [Buffalo Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Sabres "Buffalo Sabres") head coach [Lindy Ruff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindy_Ruff "Lindy Ruff"), he was claimed by the Sabres the next day, putting him and [Alexandar Georgiev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandar_Georgiev "Alexandar Georgiev") in contention for the backup spot to start the season behind [Alex Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Lyon_/(ice_hockey/) "Alex Lyon (ice hockey)").[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-45) Georgiev was waived the following day, making Ellis the backup to Lyon to start the season.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-46) Ellis made his NHL debut on October 22 in a 4–2 win against the [Detroit Red Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Red_Wings "Detroit Red Wings"), saving 27 out of 29 shots on goal.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-47)[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-48) With his debut, he became the first goaltender from [Cape Breton Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Island "Cape Breton Island") to play in the NHL, the eighth from [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia"), and the ninth Sabres goaltender to win in their debut.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-49)

For the [2018 IIHF World U18 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IIHF_World_U18_Championships "2018 IIHF World U18 Championships"), Ellis and [Olivier Rodrigue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Rodrigue "Olivier Rodrigue") were selected as the team's goaltenders. He started the first two round-robin games against the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Hockey_National_Team_Development_Program "USA Hockey National Team Development Program") and [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus_men%27s_national_under-18_ice_hockey_team "Belarus men's national under-18 ice hockey team"), recording a 3.50 GAA and a .887 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-50) Rodrigue took over the starting goaltender role and Team Canada continued in quarterfinals play, where they lost to the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_men%27s_national_under-18_ice_hockey_team "Czech Republic men's national under-18 ice hockey team").[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-51)[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-52)

Ellis was contention for the [2020 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Junior_Ice_Hockey_Championships "2020 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships") roster for [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_men%27s_national_junior_ice_hockey_team "Canada men's national junior ice hockey team"), participating in what was considered an average summer showcase, but did not make the December camp roster cut.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-53)

On December 20, 2024, [Hockey Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockey_Canada "Hockey Canada") announced their roster for the [2024 Spengler Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Spengler_Cup "2024 Spengler Cup"), which selected Ellis and [Antoine Bibeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Bibeau "Antoine Bibeau") as the goaltenders. At the time of his selection, he had an 8–4–2 record with a 2.70 GAA and a .918 save percentage.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-54) He started the tournament in net against [HC Davos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HC_Davos "HC Davos"), recording 25 saves in a 6–2 win.[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TIO-55) Ellis continued to be the starting goaltender for Team Canada, playing two more games before losing to the [Straubing Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straubing_Tigers "Straubing Tigers") in the semifinals. He finished the tournament with a second-best 2.68 GAA and a .911 save percentage, only behind HC Davos goaltender [Luca Hollenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luca_Hollenstein "Luca Hollenstein").[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TIO-55)

Six years later: Former Cape Breton Eagles head coach, GM discuss decision to trade Colten Ellis over Kevin Mandolese
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By Jeremy Fraser, PNI Atlantic

Last updated May 07, 2023

![Image 2: Kevin Mandolese of the Cape Breton Eagles, right, and Colten Ellis of the Rimouski Océanic shake hands following Game 5 of the 2019 best-of-seven second round Quebec Major Junior Hockey League playoff series between the two teams at Centre 200 in Sydney. Ellis and the Océanic won the series 4-1 and advanced to the league’s semifinal series that year. JEREMY FRASR/CAPE BRETON POST](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/six-years-later-former-cape-breton-eagles-head-coach-gm-discu_ncyvowl.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&h=216&sig=nayHBj3jrZm2ayBIjbC3YA)

Kevin Mandolese of the Cape Breton Eagles, right, and Colten Ellis of the Rimouski Océanic shake hands following Game 5 of the 2019 best-of-seven second round Quebec Major Junior Hockey League playoff series between the two teams at Centre 200 in Sydney. Ellis and the Océanic won the series 4-1 and advanced to the league’s semifinal series that year. JEREMY FRASR/CAPE BRETON POST Photo by Jeremy Fraser /Jeremy Fraser

SYDNEY, N.S. — It was one of the most discussed trades in Cape Breton Eagles history and six years later it’s still a topic of discussion among local fans.

Colten Ellis, a hometown boy who grew up an hour and a half from Sydney in River Denys, was traded to the Rimouski Océanic on June 3, 2017, for a first-round pick at the 2018 Quebec Major Junior Hockey League Entry Draft.

At the time, the 16-year-old Ellis was coming off a history-setting season with the Cape Breton West Islanders of the Nova Scotia Under-18 Major Hockey League, winning the provincial, Atlantic, and national championships, the first for an Atlantic Canadian team at the then Telus Cup.

Instead, the Eagles elected to keep goaltenders Kyle Jessiman and Kevin Mandolese, who was the club’s first round selection at the 2016 entry draft in Charlottetown.

Many questioned the decision of then-head coach and general manager Marc-André Dumont and wondered why Ellis was the odd man out of the crease and not Mandolese — both of whom were the same age and drafted in the same year.

“It was the hardest decision I had to make when in Cape Breton for seven years,” said Dumont. “Colten is an amazing young man and has an amazing family and he was a local kid.

“We took a hockey decision in the first round to draft Mandolese and obviously we weren’t the only ones to think that Mandolese was the better of the two because Colten was drafted four rounds later. If a team thought that Colten was right there, they would have picked him a few ranks later.”

### ‘Still there in fourth round’

Mandolese, a six-foot-four, 181-pound product of Blainville, Que., was selected No. 13 overall. Meanwhile, Ellis was picked in the fourth round, No. 59 overall, by Cape Breton.

“We couldn’t believe that Colten was still there in the fourth round,” said Dumont.

“My scouts at the table at the end of the second round were telling me it’s crazy that he was still available, and I told them we weren’t going to pick another goaltender in the second round after picking one in the first round, but by the fourth round we were like, ‘OK this doesn’t make sense; we have to pick him.’”

This advertisement has not loaded yet.

This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below.

Mandolese earned a roster spot out of training camp and went on to have a 16-8-0-0 record along with a 3.47 goals-against average and a .890 save percentage in 27 games with Cape Breton.

Meanwhile, Ellis returned to under-18 and Cape Breton West, posting a 13-1-0-0 record with a 2.04 goals-against average and a .930 save percentage. Ellis also appeared in two games with the Eagles as a call up.

Two months after Mandolese and the Eagles were eliminated from the second round of the playoffs by Charlottetown, the team made the decision to move on from one of their three goaltenders and moved Ellis.

“At one point we needed to move on and give a chance for both to be No. 1 goaltenders,” said Dumont. “It was very, very difficult, we really liked both goaltenders and it was tough to say that we preferred this guy to this guy.”

Dumont relieved all three of his goaltenders — Mandolese, Ellis and Jessiman — were put on the trade market following that postseason and the return for Ellis is what they ultimately decided on.

“We ended up moving two guys, but it was really hard,” said Dumont, noting Jessiman was traded a year later in 2018 to Baie-Comeau for a second-round pick.

“I’m happy that Colten had a great junior career, he ended up in a great spot and he got drafted in the NHL and he’s playing pro, so things worked out for him just like they did with Mando.”

![Image 3: Colten Ellis of River Denys spent three years with the Rimouski Ocanic after being traded to the Quebec-based team in June 2017. During his time with Rimouski, the St. Louis Blues prospect led the team to a semifinal appearance in 2019. JEREMY FRASER/CAPE BRETON POST - Jeremy Fraser](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/six-years-later-former-cape-breton-eagles-head-coach-gm-discu_yfscp9x.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=1ROWldqIKiajqPIxf0uAdA)

Colten Ellis of River Denys spent three years with the Rimouski Océanic after being traded to the Quebec-based team in June 2017. During his time with Rimouski, the St. Louis Blues prospect led the team to a semifinal appearance in 2019. JEREMY FRASER/CAPE BRETON POST – Jeremy Fraser

### How the decision was made

Dumont confirmed there were several teams who were interested in all three goaltenders.

What were the conversations among the staff at the time?

“All the hockey guys on our staff were saying, from a hockey perspective, Kevin Mandolese had a swing-span of an NHL goaltender and he was only 17 years old — we knew he could only grow, develop and could became an NHL goaltender with time,” said Dumont.

“Colten was six-foot-one and there’s teams in the NHL who don’t draft goaltenders under six-foot-two. So from a technical standpoint, it was an easy decision, but it was more on the emotional side of it having a kid from the area that can play in the QMJHL — we wanted all of them.

“We knew he would play in the QMJHL one day and we had no doubt, there was no doubt in our scouts minds that Colten Ellis would become a No. 1 goaltender in the QMJHL.”

Dumont said when the team made first-round selections in the draft and European event, the club told its scouts they wanted to draft guys who would be selected in future NHL drafts — Mandolese, Pierre-Luc Dubois, Evgeny Svechnikov, and Egor Sokolov among those.

Drake Batherson and Leon Gawanke were other players drafted outside of the first round in the QMJHL and Canadian Hockey League Import Drafts who went on to be selected at the NHL level.

“Our scouts were unanimous that, between Kevin and Colten, that Kevin was definitely the one who had the most chance of becoming an NHL goaltender,” said Dumont.

The pick acquired for Ellis was later moved to Acadie-Bathurst in 2018 to acquire Sydney product Mitchell Balmas, who had 43 goals and 82 points in 64 games with the Eagles in 2018-19.

![Image 4: Kevin Mandolese of the Cape Breton Eagles, middle, looks for the loose puck during Quebec Major Junior Hockey League action at Centre 200 in 2019. The Ottawa Senators prospect spent four years in Sydney and appeared in the playoffs in three of four seasons  the fourth was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. JEREMY FRASER/CAPE BRETON POST - Jeremy Fraser](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/six-years-later-former-cape-breton-eagles-head-coach-gm-discu_lmmeojk.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=TqsUUe121Cw-zpAZ8f2TtQ)

Kevin Mandolese of the Cape Breton Eagles, middle, looks for the loose puck during Quebec Major Junior Hockey League action at Centre 200 in 2019. The Ottawa Senators prospect spent four years in Sydney and appeared in the playoffs in three of four seasons – the fourth was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. JEREMY FRASER/CAPE BRETON POST – Jeremy Fraser

### Career breakdowns to date

Mandolese, 22, was drafted by the Ottawa Senators in the sixth round, No. 157 overall, at the 2018 NHL Entry Draft.

He spent four years with the Eagles and had his best season — statistics-wise — in 2019-20 when he posted a 26-8-1-0 record with a 2.33 goals-against average and a .925 save percentage in a COVID-19-shortened season.

Mandolese finished his major junior career with 86 victories — the second-most in the Eagles’ franchise history only behind Olivier Roy (96). He added six wins in the playoffs.

He later signed a three-year, entry-level deal with the Senators and has spent the majority of his three-year pro career to date in the American Hockey League with Belleville. He made his first career NHL start on Feb. 14, posting a 3-2 shootout win over the New York Islanders on the road.

As for Ellis, he was selected in the third round, No. 93 overall, by the St. Louis Blues. He would later sign a three-year, entry-level contract with the team.

**QMJHL CAREERS BY THE NUMBERS:  
Kevin Mandolese**  
**2016-17** – Cape Breton – Record: 16-8-0-0 – GAA: 3.47 – SV%: .890  
**2017-18** – Cape Breton – Record: 15-13-2-0 – GAA: 3.46 – SV%: .884  
**2018-19** – Cape Breton – Record: 29-12-1-4 – GAA: 2.87 – SV% .895  
**2019-20** – Cape Breton – Record: 26-8-1-0 – GAA: 2.33 – SV% .925

**Colten Ellis**  
**2016-17** – Cape Breton – Record: 2-0-0-0 – GAA: 2.50 – SV%: .885  
**2017-18** – Rimouski – Record: 33-8-5-1 – GAA: 2.35 – SV% .913  
**2018-19** – Rimouski – Record: 27-15-2-0 – GAA: 2.47 – SV% .908  
**2019-20** – Rimouski – Record: 18-7-2-1 – GAA: 2.41 – SV%: .904  
**2020-21** – Charlottetown – Record: 23-1-0-0 – GAA: 1.78 – SV%: .926

His best season — statistics-wise — came in 2020-21, when he posted a 23-1-0-0 record along with a 1.78 goals-against average and a .926 save percentage with the Charlottetown Islanders.

During the 2020-21 season, he became the first Cape Breton-born goaltender to win the QMJHL’s Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy for the best goals-against average and broke the QMJHL record for most consecutive wins to start a season (12). He later broke the league’s shutout record (18) and set the league record for lowest goals-against average.

Ellis, 22, is in his second full season of pro hockey and has spent the majority of it in the ECHL between the Worcester Railers and the Tulsa Oilers — the team he played 27 games for in 2022-23.

He has yet to play a game in the NHL.

Sabres acquire Ellis off waivers
================================

by AHL PR

October 6, 2025October 6, 2025

![Image 99](https://theahl.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/10/ellis_colten251006.jpg)Photo: Lucas Armstrong

The Buffalo Sabres have claimed goaltender [**Colten Ellis**](https://theahl.com/stats/player/8902) off waivers from the St. Louis Blues.

Ellis is coming off a career year with the AHL’s Springfield Thunderbirds, going 22-14-3 with a 2.63 goals-against average, a .922 save percentage (ranked fourth in the AHL) and three shutouts in 42 games in 2024-25.

A third-round pick by the Blues in the 2019 NHL Draft, Ellis has appeared in 64 AHL games over his first four pro seasons, going 30-26-5 with a 2.82 GAA, a .919 save percentage and three shutouts.

Tagged: [Rochester Americans](https://theahl.com/tag/rochester-americans), [Springfield Thunderbirds](https://theahl.com/tag/springfield-thunderbirds)

20.content:
The Sabres opted for a roster shakeup today as they waived goaltender Alexandar Georgiev and claimed goaltender Colten Ellis off waivers from the St. Louis Blues. Georgiev’s previous relationship with Lindy Ruff was apparently not enough to convince the team to stick with him after his dismal .824 save percentage outing against the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday. With presumptive starter Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen week-to-week, it looks like the newly acquired goaltender could even see some action during the early going of the season.

Ellis is an intriguing player. A 2019 third-round pick, he has some quality goaltending stats going back to his QMJHL days with the Charlottetown Islanders as he led the league in save percentage (.924) during the 2020-2021 campaign, according to stats from Quanthockey. He was ninth in league save percentage the year before with Rimouski Oceanic.

Since then, the now 25-year-old has bounced between the ECHL and the AHL. It seems like he really found his footing last season with the Springfield Thunderbirds as he finished the season with a .922 save percentage through 42 games. While he’s definitely on the smaller side at 6’1”, he’s not so small that he would be a complete anomaly at the NHL level; Juuse Saros is 5’11” after all.

This is a smart and somewhat gutsy move for the Sabres who need to be proactive in their approach to improving the roster at every available opportunity due to their relative lack of high-end talent compared to the upper echelon teams in the NHL. Georgiev was clearly limited in the upside that he offered the Sabres while Ellis offers significantly more potential even though he has yet to play an NHL game. The Blues clearly took the opposite approach and decided that the veteran experience of Jordan Binnington and Joel Hofer is worth more to them than the potential of Ellis. We’ll see if Ellis is able to pay off the Sabres for their gamble.

As for when the Sabres might use Ellis, that’s a trickier question to answer. There’s a potential that UPL could be back within a week or two of the home opener, but because they do have three games in five nights beginning Saturday, next Monday’s home matinee against the Avalanche a possibility for Ellis if UPL isn't ready to go.

\--------------------------------------------------------------

The Sabres will open their 2025-26 campaign this Thursday at home against the cross-state counterpart New York Rangers. Let’s dispense with the formalities and get to the point here: this game is a must-win for the Sabres.

Yes, that is a dramatic statement, and yes, they will have 81 more games to make up the standings points, but with a fan base that is ready to ignore this team the second they look like they’ve looked for the vast majority of the past 14 years, it is imperative that they not only look good, but that they win while looking good. Any talk of a moral victory or style points in defeat will likely fall on deaf ears from the fans.

Last year started with two brutal shellackings at the hands of the New Jersey Devils in Prague and the team and fans never recovered from it. Lindy Ruff, during his semi-weekly appearance on WGR550 this morning had a more medium-term approach to the season.

“If you go 3-and-2, and 3-and-2, and you get six points every five games, you’re going to be a playoff team,” Ruff said.

That is certainly true – it would be roughly a 98-point pace. What you don’t want to do is start a season 0-1 or 0-2 and then have to rattle off three wins just to get yourself back on track less than a week into the season. This first game is going to be enormous.

The Rangers are also not a powerhouse squad at this point in their timeline with some players like Mika Zibenejad starting to age out and younger players like former first overall pick Alexis Lafreniere failing to meet his lofty draft status. And while the Rangers have attempted to fortify their group with a player like JT Miller, he too is getting older and may not be a sufficient needle mover for them.

If the Sabres want to show they’re for real this time, the Rangers are a good place to find their first win of the season.

FORMER RAILER COLTEN ELLIS MAKES NHL DEBUT
==========================================

 ![Image 5: FORMER RAILER COLTEN ELLIS MAKES NHL DEBUT](https://echl.imgix.net/production/wor/post/1423/featured_image/226f9164-0c00-48e1-8107-f795398cf8cb/coltenellis.jpg?ar=16%3A9&auto=compress%2Cformat&crop=faces%2Ccenter&fit=crop&w=1200&s=d5b2639dcb29656f55cb27b2baf8481d)

**FORMER RAILER COLTEN ELLIS MAKES NHL DEBUT**

Ellis is fifth Railer to appear in NHL after playing in Worcester.

**WORCESTER, Mass.** – The **Worcester Railers Hockey Club** ([@RailersHC](https://twitter.com/RailersHC)), proud **ECHL** ([@ECHL](https://twitter.com/ECHL)) affiliate of the **New York Islanders** ([@NYIslanders](https://twitter.com/NYIslanders)), announced today that former goaltender **Colten Ellis** has become the 770th player in ECHL history to make his NHL debut after appearing in an ECHL game with his appearance against the Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday night.

**Ellis**, 25, played in 34 games for the Railers during the 2021-22 season. In his rookie season with Worcester, the River Denys, NS native had a .905 save-percentage to go with a 3.21 goals against average and a 15-13-5 record. Ellis has made additional stops across the ECHL with the Tulsa Oilers and Orlando Solar Bears. Ellis has played in 64 games for the American Hockey League's Springfield Thunderbirds across three seasons before being claimed off of waivers by the Buffalo Sabres on October 6th, 2025. He was taken by the St. Louis Blues in the third round (93rd overall) of the 2019 NHL Entry Draft.

The 6'1", 185lb goaltender is the fifth Railer player to go on to play in the NHL after appearing in a game for Worcester. He joins **Tristan Lennox**, who made his NHL debut for the Islanders on April 10th, 2025, **Jakub Skarek**, who made his NHL debut for the Islanders on February 2nd, 2025, **Arnaud Durandeau**, who made his NHL debut for the Islanders on February 20th, 2023, and **Ken Appleby**, who appeared in one game for the Islanders on January 15th, 2024.

19.content: ST. LOUIS -- The [St. Louis Blues](http://thn.com/stlouis) lost goalie Colten Ellis, who was claimed off waivers by the [Buffalo Sabres](http://thn.com/buffalo) on Monday. The 25-year-old, a 2019 third-round pick, would have been the starting goalie at Springfield of the American Hockey League but required waivers in order to be sent down. The Sabres are in need of current reinforcements with Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen out week-to-week with a lower-body injury. With Jordan Binnington and Joel Hofer entrenched as the 1-2 punch in St. Louis, the Blues were hoping to get Ellis through. The Blues, however, could get Ellis back in the organization once the Sabres get UPL back from injury and re-expose Ellis on waivers. The only edge they could get is if they re-claim him, they don't ha e to keep him in the NHL and could assign Ellis immediately to Springfield. It would be a regular waiver claim process, so other teams could have dibs before the Blues so we will see how this goes. In the meantime, Vadim Zherenko becomes Springfield's No. 1 goalie, with Will Cranley as the backup. Also, Hunter Skinner cleared waivers and will head to Springfield; the defenseman made a strong case for himself in training camp to be the seventh defenseman, but Matthew Kessel won over the job. Colten Ellis shines as Canada’s goalie at Spengler Cup
------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1](https://invernessoran.ca/images/slideshow_2025_01/Jan8-25Sports.jpg)

_Colten Ellis faced 44 shots in the Spengler Cup semifinal against Straubing and finished the tournament with a .911 save percentage. He’s shown here making a save with defenceman Jonathan Aspirot looking on._

* * *

January 8, 2025

\-by Bill Dunphy  
    Colten Ellis did what he does best as Team Canada’s goaltender at the Spengler Cup tournament in Davos, Switzerland – gave his team a chance to win.  
    Unfortunately, his best fell short of Team Canada winning a medal, despite an outstanding performance by Ellis, especially in their semifinal match against the Straubing (Germany) Tigers.  
    The six-team invitational tournament was held from Dec. 26-31. First held in 1923, the Spengler Cup is often cited as the oldest invitational ice hockey tournament in the world. Canada and the host team Davos have each won the cup 16 times.  
    Team Canada is comprised of Canadians predominantly playing in Europe, as well as players from the American Hockey League and the East Coast Hockey League. The other five teams are all club teams playing in Europe.  
    Ellis, a St. Louis Blues prospect who plays for the AHL’s Springfield Thunderbirds, is 8-4-2 with a 2.70 goals-against average and a .918 save percentage. Before leaving for Davos, he was 6-0-2 in his last eight starts with a 2.59 GAA and .923 save percentage.  
    While Canada had three goaltenders on its roster, coach Gerard Gallant went with Ellis to start the tournament and wasn’t disappointed.  
    In the opening game of the group stage, Ellis turned aside 25 of the 27 shots he faced as Canada defeated Davos 6-2.  
    Gallant stayed with Ellis in game two, with Canada defeating Straubing 6-3. Shots were 28-20 in favour of Canada. All three of Straubing’s goals were scored on the powerplay, including one on a five-on-three.  
    Of note, the only other Cape Bretoner on the team, Glace Bay’s Logan Shaw, scored twice in the game.  
    Canada was the only team to win both of its group stage games and advanced directly to the semifinals. Straubing had to play a quarterfinal game against Dynamo Pardubice, beating the Czechia club 5-0 to advance to the semifinal against Canada on Monday, Dec. 30.  
    Straubing got the jump on Canada with a powerplay goal in the first period.  
    Canada tied it five minutes later and took a 2-1 lead with a powerplay goal in the second.  
    Straubing tied it before the period’s end, setting up a tense third period, made even more tense when Canada’s Curtis McKenzie took a four-minute high sticking penalty three minutes in.  
    And for the next four minutes, Ellis made save after save – 12 in total – prompting the TSN announcer to exclaim, “Ellis saves Canada!”  
    Ellis saw 18 shots in the third period alone, 44 in total, but it was the flukiest of shots that ended up beating him.  
    At 9:04. Straubing’s Joshua Samanski was breaking into the Canada zone and Ellis came out of the crease to cut the angle. Samanski’s shot deflected off a Canadian defender and the puck flipped 12 feet into the air only to fall into the net behind Ellis.  
    Straubing would go on to score an empty-net goal to win the game 4-2.  
    In an Oran interview after his return to Springfield, Ellis said it was a tough way to lose.  
    “It was the kind of play that when it happens, it sucks, but you don’t think of it in the moment. There was still 10 minutes left to play, and our team played really well, but we couldn’t get it back.”  
    Other than that, Ellis said he enjoyed his second international experience playing for Canada, having been to Russia in 2018 at the U18 World Hockey Championship.  
    “It was an amazing experience. Everybody was great as was the camaraderie among the team,” he said, adding it was cool to play every game.  
    “I didn’t find out I would be starting the first game until I got there. We won it, and it went from there.”  
    Ellis said it took a little adjustment to get used to the larger ice surface.  
    “Definitely, playing on the larger ice surface is a little different for everybody. Trigger points and angles are a little different, but we had a couple of practices to get used to it.”  
    Ellis had eight goals against in the three games, four of which were scored on powerplays. He finished the tournament with a .911 save percentage and a 2.68 goals-against average, second only to Davos goalie Luca Hollenstein’s 1.50 GAA in just two games played.  
    Davos goalie Zane McIntyre was named to the tournament all-star team despite finishing third behind Ellis with a 3.00 GAA and a .905 save percentage.  
    Even though the Thunderbirds are on break until Jan. 11, Ellis said there was no time to spend at home in River Denys.  
    “It was tough to leave at this time of the year and I wanted to get back with the guys. We have a good team here and even though we don’t play until next week, we don’t have much down time. We’ll get a day off and then its practice every day.”  
    Ellis thanked everyone who showed their support during his time in Switzerland, including those who made the trip, which included his dad Brian, uncle Wendell, his girl friend Hannah MacDonald, her dad Grant, her uncle Kevin, as well as some family friends.

By St. Louis Blues / Press Release

December 20, 2024

*   Link copied

Hockey Canada announced today that Springfield Thunderbirds goaltender Colten Ellis has been named to its roster for the upcoming 2024 Spengler Cup. The Spengler Cup is an annual international invitational hockey tournament held in Davos, Switzerland from December 26-31. It is often cited as the oldest international invitational ice hockey tournament in the world.

Ellis, 24, has appeared in 14 games for the Thunderbirds this season, posting an 8-4-2 record along with a 2.70 goals-against average and a .918 save percentage. His eight wins this season share 8th in the AHL while his .918 save percentage ranks 8th.

Overall, the River Denys, Nova Scotia, native has played in 36 career AHL games, recording a 16-16-6 record with a 2.99 goals-against average and a .915 save percentage.

This will be Ellis’ second time representing Team Canada after appearing in the 2018 U-18 World Junior Championship.

![Image 1](https://www.buffalohockeybeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Ellis3.jpg) Colten Ellis made 27 saves Wednesday. ©2025, Micheline Veluvolu

BUFFALO – In the opening minutes of a goalie’s NHL debut, facing a shot or two and simply feeling the puck can help him calm any nerves and settle into the game.

So as [Sabres goalie Colten Ellis](https://www.buffalohockeybeat.com/sabres-notes-colten-ellis-standing-out-in-buffalo-will-get-chance-to-play/) waited and waited for his first chance to make a save on Wednesday, it was fair to wonder how he would react.

Well, Ellis, a recent waiver claim who backed up veteran Alex Lyon in the Sabres’ first six games, responded when the Detroit Red Wings finally challenged him in KeyBank Center.

Ellis, 25, stopped the first shot Detroit pumped on him 6:59 into the contest, a 27-foot wrister from old friend Jacob Bernard-Docker, and looked sharp throughout the Sabres’ 4-2 victory that ended Detroit’s five-game win streak.

The rookie was perhaps Sabres’ biggest difference-maker, making some critical, momentum-swinging stops in a tight game.

“The boys came out strong, and they were playing so good, and I was kind of like, ‘Gee, I need a shot here at some point to get me into it a little bit,’” Ellis said following his splendid 27-save effort. “But I can’t commend them enough for all the effort tonight.”

Ellis stymied Marco Kasper’s breakaway late in the first period to keep the game tied at 0 and Dylan Larkin’s breakaway out of the penalty box early in the second to keep the Sabres down just 1-0.

“Got a little concerned because (he faced) no shots for the longest period of time,” said coach Lindy Ruff, whose Sabres have won three of their last four games. “One of the first big chances he faces is a breakaway and makes a heck of a save, and I think that alone probably made him feel good.”

Winger Jason Zucker tied the game at 11:37, converting a nifty pass from linemate Jack Quinn. Forward Tyson Kozak gave the Sabres their first lead at 16:28.

After Quinn’s power-play goal 4:15 into the third period put the Sabres up 3-2, Ellis slid across the crease and stopped Alex DeBrincat’s point-blank shot on his doorstep about five minutes later.

At 8:10, winger Josh Doan scored, giving the Sabres a two-goal cushion.

“Those are the type of saves of you build off of,” Ruff said. “You get a big save, and then a lot of times you go down the other way and score. Bench was fired up. The crowd was fired up when you see a save like that. So it was a big momentum swing in the game.”

Ellis said “you fuel on moments like that in the game.”

After the Sabres added Ellis, Ruff said the newcomer would play. Then Lyon thrived with his heavy workload as No. 1 goalie Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen recovered from his lower-body injury.

It seemed like Lyon, who spent the last two seasons with Detroit, might face his old team. But the Sabres decided he needed a rest.

“Just too many games for Lyon,” Ruff said of why Ellis started Wednesday. “Really, we just felt we reached a point. No more than that. Nothing to do with him and Detroit or anything. Really, it got to a point where we just felt we’ve got a busy week, and we have to get him in.”

For Ellis, who toiled in the St. Louis Blues’ system for four years, spending most of his his time in the ECHL, Wednesday was a magical day.

The Whycocomagh, Nova Scotia, native said he had 25 to 30 supporters in the crowd of 15,104 fans.

“I was pretty emotional before the game,” he said. “Me and my fiancée were sitting in the hotel and found some old pictures of me playing hockey. Kind of didn’t really expect that for myself.

“Just, obviously, ecstatic to have all my family here and so many supporters here. It’s so special to get to share this moment with them.”

TNT cameras showed his mother nervously watching him throughout the night.

“She’s usually a wreck,” Ellis said. “She got through it, so good for her, but she definitely gets picked on for that.”

The Sabres finished the game down a forward after Zucker left late in the second period with an upper-body injury. Ruff said he was being evaluated and did not have an update.

Quinn assisted on the first two goals and had a three-point night.

Colten Ellis wins the 2020-21 Jacques-Plante Trophy
---------------------------------------------------

Category: [Article](https://chl.ca/lhjmq-islanders/category/article/)[June 4, 2021](https://chl.ca/lhjmq-islanders/2021/06/04/ "2:00 pm")

The Quebec Major Junior Hockey League highlighted today the top goaltender of the 2020-2021 campaign.

The Jacques-Plante Memorial Trophy is awarded annually to the goaltender who maintained the best goals-against-average. It is named after Hockey Hall of Famer and Shawinigan native Jacques Plante, who certainly left his mark on hockey history.

Past recipients of the award include several NHL alumni netminders such as Félix Potvin, Jocelyn Thibault and Martin Biron, to name a few.

Former QMJHL and NHL goaltender Jocelyn Thibault is the one who announced this year’s Jacques-Plante Trophy winner.

The 2020-2021 recipient of the award is Colten Ellis of the Charlottetown Islanders. The overage player enjoyed a season for the ages. He won 23 games and suffered just one loss while establishing a new league record with a 1.78 goals-against-average.

Ellis also posted an excellent 0.926% save percentage during the campaign. The Antigonish, NS native also established another QMJHL record for most career shutouts with 17.

Ellis was a third round selection, 93rd overall, of the St-Louis Blues during the 2019 NHL Entry Draft. He signed his first professional contract with the organization back in March.
