Colten Ellis signs entry-level deal with St. Louis Blues
--------------------------------------------------------

Category: [Article](https://chl.ca/lhjmq-islanders/category/article/)[March 1, 2021](https://chl.ca/lhjmq-islanders/2021/03/01/ "4:27 pm")

The St. Louis Blues announced today that they have signed Charlottetown Islanders goaltender Colten Ellis to a three-year entry level contract that will begin with the 2021-22 season.

Ellis, 20, was originally drafted by the Blues in the third round (93rd overall) of the 2019 NHL Draft. He was selected in the same draft as former Islander Nikita Alexandrov.

This season, Ellis has played in 17 games thus far, recording a 16-1-0 record and leading the league in wins. His 1.89 goals-against average ranks second and his .922 save-percentage ranks third, while he also has recorded five shutouts.

The 6-foot-1, 187-pound goaltender has split the past four seasons with the Islanders and Rimouski Oceanic, posting a 96-31-11 record with a career 2.35 goals-against average and a .911 save-percentage in 146 career games. He was originally selected by the Cape Breton Eagles in the 2016 QMJHL Draft.

In 2017-18, Ellis was named to the QMJHL All-Rookie team and the Second All-Star team.

From the entire Charlottetown Islanders organization, we’d like to congratulate Colten on his new contract!

UPDATE: Colten Ellis sets new QMJHL record for career shutouts
--------------------------------------------------------------

By Jason Malloy, PNI Atlantic

Last updated Mar 22, 2021

![Image 2: Charlottetown Islanders goalie Colten Ellis is now second all-time in career shutouts in the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League after blanking Halifax on Wednesday.](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/dsc8351_xtijtet-3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&h=216&sig=IY2YokAEZTtDh41FU-8q1g)

Charlottetown Islanders goalie Colten Ellis is now second all-time in career shutouts in the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League after blanking Halifax earlier this year. - Jason Malloy Photo by Jason Malloy /Jason Malloy

SYDNEY, N.S. — Colten Ellis has more career shutouts than any goalie to ever play in the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League.  
The 20-year-old native of River Denys, N.S., set the record against the team that drafted him Sunday, 90 minutes from his hometown.  
Ellis made 22 saves as the Charlottetown Islanders blanked the Cape Breton Eagles 4-0 in Sydney, N.S.  
“It’s definitely pretty special,” Ellis said Sunday night. “I definitely wouldn’t have got to where I am now this year without the group in front of me.”  
It was his 18th career shutout, surpassing Philippe Cadorette’s mark set with Baie-Comeau and Shawinigan from 2012-16.  
“It kind of played out perfectly. I had a lot of family and friends there today,” Ellis said. “It was nice to achieve it with all of them in the stands.”

### Record setter

Here’s a look at the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League’s all-time career shutouts leaders.  
Player, team Season Shutouts  
Colten Ellis, Rimouski/Charlottetown 2016-21 18  
Philippe Cadorette, Baie-Comeau/Shawinigan 2012-16 17  
Alex Dubeau, Shawinigan/Moncton 2010-15 16  
Louis-Philip Guindon, Drummondville/Rimouski 2012-16 15  
Samuel Harvey, Rouyn-Noranda 2014-19 15  
Ryan Mior, P.E.I./Gatineau 2003-08 15  
Olivier Roy, Cape Breton/Acadie-Bathurst 2017-11 14  
Christopher Gibson, Chicoutimi 2009-13 13  
Matthew Welsh, Charlottetown 2015-20 13  
Olivier Rodrigue, Drummondville/Moncton 2016-20 13  
Zachary Fucale, Halifax/Quebec 2011-15 13  
Adam Russo, Acadie-Bathurst 2000-04 13

Seven of Ellis’ shutouts have come this season with the Islanders, who acquired the St. Louis Blues prospect from the Rimouski Oceanic at the draft in June.  
Islanders defenceman Noah Laaouan knew first-hand how good a goalie they were getting. Ellis and his Cape Breton West Islanders defeated Laaouan and his Steele Subaru squad in the 2017 Nova Scotia under-18 final and Cape Breton West went on to win the Telus Cup national championship.  
Laaouan said Ellis’ statistics speak for themselves but only tell part of the story.  
“People don’t see the work ethic and the little things he does off the ice that really put him over the top,” Laaouan said Monday, noting how happy his teammates were for him. “I think everything that he has earned so far is rightfully deserved.”  
The veteran netminder quickly became part of the Islanders’ family after arriving for training camp.  
“His personality and work ethic is something that rubs off on everybody,” Laaouan said. “When you have those two things combined, it makes it really easy for him to fit in.”  
Laaouan said there wasn’t much talk about the record heading into Sunday’s game.  
“As the game got on, there might have been a little bit of a growing sense it could happen last night, and sure enough it did,” he said.  
Laaouan also pointed out Ellis set the record while only playing three games in the league as a 16-year-old with the Eagles. Cape Breton traded him to Rimouski in the off-season, and he starred for the Oceanic for three seasons, including earning 33 wins and six shutouts in his rookie campign.  
His time in Rimouski, Que., means a lot to Ellis.  
“I got to play with a lot of great players and meet a lot of great people,” he said. “The organization was just awesome right from the start.”  
Keiran Gallant, Bailey Peach, Ben Boyd and Laaouan scored for the Islanders on Sunday. Lukas Cormier had three assists while Laaouan had a pair and singles went to Oscar Plandowski, Cédric Desruisseaux and Thomas Casey.  
Desruisseaux extended his point streak to 16 games and is one behind the league’s longest streak of the season, set by former Cape Breton forward Shawn Element.  
Nicolas Ruccia stopped 30 shots in the loss.  
The Islanders, who held 1-0 and 3-0 period leads, improved to a league-leading 27-4-0-0 and have won 12 straight games. Cape Breton is 12-20-1-0.  
The Islanders host the Halifax Mooseheads (11-15-4-3) Saturday at 7 p.m. and the Eagles Sunday at 4 p.m. The Islanders last 20 games have come against their Nova Scotia rivals due to COVID-19 restrictions. Previous to that, Charlottetown defeated Moncton 6-4 on Nov. 7.

Jason Malloy is The Guardian’s sports editor. He can be reached by email at [jason.malloy@theguardian.pe.ca](http://jason.malloy@theguardian.pe.ca/) and followed on Twitter at [@SportsGuardian](https://twitter.com/SportsGuardian) .

Colten Ellis, who is from Whycocomagh, N.S., and plays for the Charlottetown Islanders, broke one QMJHL record over the weekend and is on the verge of breaking another.

Colten Ellis on verge of breaking another league goalie record
--------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1: Text to Speech Icon](https://www.cbc.ca/a/assets/texttospeech.svg)

Listen to this article

Estimated 4 minutes

The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

![Image 2](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5959098,1616430512000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C121%2C2040%2C1147%29%3B)

Colten Ellis, who plays for the Charlottetown Islanders, is at the top of all the QMJHL goalie statistical categories. (Darrell Theriault)

Colten Ellis of Whycocomagh, N.S., broke one QMJHL record over the weekend and is on the verge of breaking another.

When his team, the Charlottetown Islanders, beat the Cape Breton Eagles 4-0 on Sunday at Centre 200 in Sydney, N.S., Ellis registered his 18th QMJHL shutout, more than any other goaltender in the history of the league.

"It was pretty special because it obviously wasn't something I had my sights on when I came into the league," said Ellis. "Even coming into this year I don't even think I knew what the record was."

The 20-year-old now has seven shutouts this season and needs just one more to break the league's single-season shutout record, which is currently held by six goalies, including longtime NHL star Roberto Luongo.

![Image 3](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5959097,1616430442000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1270%2C1096%29%3B)

Ellis, right, looks around Cape Breton Eagles forward Jack Campbell and Islanders defenceman Sean Stewart during action Sunday at Centre 200 in Sydney, N.S. (Mike Sullivan)

The shutout over the weekend was extra sweet for Ellis because his record-breaking night came in Cape Breton, where Whycocomagh is located.

"I had lots of family and friends in attendance," said Ellis. "Every time we play in Cape Breton I feel it's like a home game for me."

Ellis spent the majority of his junior career in Rimouski but was traded to Charlottetown to replace longtime Islanders goalie Matthew Welsh, now at Saint Mary's University.

Ellis has had an outstanding season and is the league leader in goals-against average, save percentage, wins and shutouts. But the St. Louis Blues draft pick — Ellis signed a three-year deal with the Blues three weeks ago — is quick to praise his defence.

There are three more Nova Scotians on the Charlottetown blue line. Ellis said Noah Laaouan and Oscar Plandowski of Halifax, and Sean Stewart of Antigonish have all been key players in the team's success this season. Stewart played midget hockey with Ellis in Cape Breton.

![Image 4](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5959099,1616430718000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1024%2C576%29%3B)

Ellis signed a three-year contract with the St. Louis Blues three weeks ago. (Instagram)

The Islanders have been head and shoulders above everyone else in the QMJHL Maritimes division this season. With 27 wins in 31 games, they also have the best winning percentage in the entire league.

"Being able to join this team was pretty awesome for me," said Ellis. "I definitely knew that they would contend and were looking to make a run for the championship, and so far it's been a great year."

The 2020-21 season has been an unusual one to say the least. Quebec-based teams cannot play in the Maritimes due to COVID-19 restrictions. All three Maritime provinces have been impacted by ongoing restrictions that postponed many games and backed up the league schedule.

![Image 5](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5959100,1616430653000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C77%2C1638%2C1384%29%3B)

Ellis is just one shutout away from setting a second QMJHL record. (Darrell Theriault)

The QMJHL has yet to announce its playoff plan. The season is expected to continue for several more weeks, with playoffs expected to start some time in mid-to-late April. It's still to be determined if there will be a Memorial Cup championship tournament played. The Ontario Hockey League has not played any games yet this season, but a startup appears close.

While Ellis has had an outstanding junior career, he may be best known for a historic win that came four seasons ago. At the 2017 Telus Cup, the national midget hockey championship, Ellis led his Cape Breton West Islanders to the gold medal game in Prince George, BC.

![Image 6](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5959101,1616430797000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C780%2C439%29%3B)

Colten Ellis, front row, far right, was one of the key players for the Cape Breton West Islanders when they won the 2017 Telus Cup championship in British Columbia. (Matthew Murnaghan/Hockey Canada)

In the championship game he made 43 saves, including 22 in the third period and a breakaway save in overtime to lead his team to victory. It was the first time a Nova Scotia team won a national midget hockey title.

"For us to go out there and do what we did, it was pretty incredible," said Ellis, who said he remains in contact with many of his old teammates. "Especially for me coming from a small town in Cape Breton."

River Denys’ Colten Ellis becomes first Cape Breton product to win QMJHL’s Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Ellis won the award with his 1.78 goals-against-average with the Charlottetown Islanders last season

By Jeremy Fraser, PNI Atlantic

Last updated Jun 04, 2021

![Image 2: River Denys’ Colten Ellis and the Charlottetown Islanders are currently playing the Acadie-Bathurst Titan in the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League Maritime Division final. The Islanders finished first overall in the six-team Maritime Division. JEREMY FRASER/CAPE BRETON POST](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/cape-bretons-colten-ellis-lane-hinkley-square-off-in-qmjhl-ma_brwfrbd-2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&h=216&sig=bB1-FIj1BX_v17Md0sTDrQ)

River Denys’ Colten Ellis was awarded the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy by the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League on Friday. JEREMY FRASER/CAPE BRETON POST Photo by Jeremy Fraser /Jeremy Fraser

SYDNEY, N.S. – A River Denys goaltender etched his name in the Cape Breton hockey record books on Friday.

Colten Ellis was the recipient of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League’s Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy for the 2020-21 season, becoming the first Cape Breton product to win the award.

The trophy is awarded annually to the goaltender who maintained the best goals-against-average and is named after hockey hall of famer Jacques Plante.

The award doesn’t come as a surprise for the 20-year-old Ellis. The St. Louis Blues prospect set a league record for the lowest goals-against-average (1.78) with the Charlottetown Islanders in April.

Ellis is among notable Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy winners including Félix Potvin (Chicoutimi – 1990-91), Jocelyn Thibault (Sherbrooke – 1992-93), Martin Biron (Beauport – 1994-95), Marc Denis (Chicoutimi – 1996-97), Mathieu Garon (Victoriaville – 1997-98), and Jake Allen (Drummondville – 2009-10).

![Image 3: Colten Ellis and the Charlottetown Islanders will open their Quebec Major Junior Hockey League semifinal series against the Victoriaville Tigres today. The River Denys product has been to the league semifinal once before with the Rimouski Ocanic. JEREMY FRASER  CAPE BRETON POST - Jeremy Fraser](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/colten-ellis-charlottetown-islanders-begin-qmjhl-semifinals-_4b5ee1o-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=o3y_QlJy1U3dYvQ6y3zf_A)

Colten Ellis is shown during Quebec Major Junior Hockey League action at Centre 200 in April. JEREMY FRASER • CAPE BRETON POST – Jeremy Fraser

During the season, Ellis set various franchise and league records with Charlottetown.

In November, Ellis set an Islanders’ record for consecutive wins (8), breaking the team’s previous record of seven straight victories held by Matthew Welsh.

Meanwhile, in February, Ellis broke the QMJHL record for most consecutive wins to start a season (12). He later broke the league’s shutout record (18), passing Philippe Cadorette who had 17 shutouts during his career between Baie-Comeau and Shawinigan.

During the 2020-21 regular season, Ellis had a 23-1-0-0 record with a .926 save percentage. He finishes his major junior career with a total of 119 wins and 53 losses between Cape Breton, Rimouski and Charlottetown.

Two Cape Breton Eagles players were victorious in winning the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy since 1997.

Martin Houle was the first Eagles player to win the trophy with his 2.32 goals-against-average during the 2003-04 season. Meanwhile, Ondrej Pavelec won the trophy in both 2005-06 and 2006-07 with his 2.51 and 2.52 goals-against-average records.

Prior to Ellis, the last Nova Scotian to win the trophy was Halifax’s Chase Marchand with a 2.42 goals-against-average during the 2015-16 season with the Rouyn-Noranda Huskies.

Michel Deguise of the Sorel Éperviers was the first-ever recipient of the trophy with his 3.99 goals-against-average during the 1969-70 season. Ironically, the Éperviers are now the Eagles.

_**– Jeremy Fraser is the sports reporter for the Cape Breton Post. Follow Jeremy on Twitter [@CBPost\_Jeremy.](http://www.twitter.com/CBPost_Jeremy)**_

NHL hopeful Colten Ellis keeps his eye on the prize
---------------------------------------------------

![Image 1](https://www.invernessoran.ca/images/slideshow_2022_01/Jan19-22Sports.jpg)

_Colten Ellis, of River Denys, is navigating his way to an NHL career while playing for the Springfield Thunderbirds of the AHL and the Worcester Railers of the ECHL – both affiliated teams with the St. Louis Blues._

* * *

January 19, 2022

\-by Bill Dunphy  
    Getting drafted by a National Hockey League team is a highlight of any hockey player’s career – to a point.  
    Making that NHL team is a different story.  
    And that’s the story Colten Ellis is writing now.  
    Ellis, who hails from River Denys, is a third-round pick of the St. Louis Blues. He signed a three-year entry-level contract in March 2021 valued at $2,775,000 – should he play with St. Louis – and which pays him a salary of $70,000 a year in the minors.

After a strong showing at the Blues’ training camp, the 21-year-old goaltender was then designated to play with Blue’s affiliate teams, the Springfield Thunderbirds of the American Hockey League and the Worcester Railers of the East Coast Hockey League.  
    Ellis has nine games played with the Railers and has a won-lost-tied record of 4-3-1, a goals-against average of 3.30 and a .905 save percentage.  
    He is currently in Springfield where he has played six games, compiling a 1-3-3 record, 3.76 GAA and a .884 save percentage.  
    Not since 1998, when Inverness power forward Randy Copley was drafted in the second round by the New York Rangers, has an Inverness County player come this close to achieving what Allan MacInnis did in 1981 when he started his all-star career with the Calgary Flames.  
    But as he has done throughout his career, Ellis remains focused on the job at hand. Since he was assigned to Springfield in October, Ellis has gone back and forth to Worcester six times.  
    “It’s a lot different and an adjustment for me,” said Ellis last Tuesday in Worcester, a day before getting called up to the Thunderbirds.  
    “They are two completely different organizations, so it’s an adjustment playing with guys from two different structures. But at the end of the day, hockey is hockey. You show up and do your job.”  
    In comparison, the day before interviewing Ellis, former Halifax Mooseheads star goaltender Zach Fucale had set a franchise record for scoreless minutes with the Washington Capitals before the Boston Bruins scored four times on 16 shots to effectively send him back to his AHL team, the Hershey Bears.  
    Fucale, who is five years older than Ellis, was a second-round draft pick of the Montreal Canadiens in 2013. Since then, after finishing his Junior career, he has played for 11 different AHL and ECHL teams before getting four starts with Washington.  
    “I was a big fan of his growing up,” said Ellis. “It’s cool to see his story and how his resiliency paid off. But everyone has a different path. It can be hard at times, if you’re not in the right mind-set.  
    “I’m working towards the bigger goal and focussed on just getting better.”  
    Ellis knows that hockey at the professional level is a business, but he said the fun of hockey is still there.  
    “The first half of the season was a whirlwind, but I’m having fun and enjoying it.”  
    Two highlights that still stand out for him include a pre-season game on Oct. 1 with St. Louis in which the Blues defeated the Chicago Blackhawks 6-3 and his first game in the AHL.  
    “Both were big wins for me. It was pretty awesome and makes you want to work even harder,” he said.  
    In his NHL debut, Ellis gave up just one goal (Ryan Carpenter) on seven shots. In the minute leading up to that goal, Ellis made consecutive saves on Patrick Kane (14:54), Jake McCabe (15:14) and Tyler Johnson (15:17). On that save, the puck went back to the neutral zone, but a pair of takeaways by Dylan Strome led to the goal at 15:58.  
    Ellis managed to get home during Christmas to spend time with his parents, Joanne and Brian, and his brother Matt.  
    “It’s always good to get home, recharge the batteries, and spend time with family and friends. Getting a few home-cooked meals doesn’t hurt either.”  
    The AHL’s regular season ends on April 30. The ECHL’s regular season ends on April 17.  
    Where Ellis will play depends on how he makes use of the next three months.  
    “It’s going to be hectic. It’s most beneficial for me to try and get better with each game I play.”  
    For the guy who won a Telus Cup National Midget title with the Cape Breton West Islanders and owns the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League all-time shutout record of 18 (tied the record of seven in one season) while playing with the Charlottetown Islanders, getting better each game is what he does best.

Buffalo Sabres face another blow as rookie goalie Colten Ellis lands on injured reserve with a concussion. This setback intensifies their struggle for playoff contention, placing immense pressure on their remaining goaltenders. With the longest playoff drought in the NHL, Ellis's absence significantly narrows their margin for error during this crucial season phase.

![Image 2: NHL Injury Update: Colten Ellis placed on IR as Buffalo Sabres face another major setback](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-125920010,imgsize-41718,width-400,resizemode-4/colten-ellis.jpg)

Colten Ellis (Image Via Twitter)

The most recent NHL injury update, Buffalo Sabres news, and Colten Ellis injury report have captured the headlines as the team suffers another setback in their heated Eastern Conference battle. Every roster change matters, and the coming of the IR for Ellis has become a huge talking point in the league as the Sabres are trying to break the record of their long-term postseason drought.Rookie goalie Colten Ellis was placed on the injured reserve list after a concussion spotter removed him during the Tuesday 4-3 win against the Edmonton Oilers. Before leaving, he had stopped all six shots taken at him and was having a very promising start to his very first NHL season. Claimed off waivers from St.Louis in October, Ellis has got 4-3-0 in eight games with a .895 SV% and 3.25 GAA, showing moments of his AHL form where he had a very strong .922 SV% last year in Springfield.

What does injury to Colten Ellis mean for Buffalo Sabres' already fragile season?
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Buffalo is hit by Ellis' injury at the very moment when they are struggling the most. The Sabres are at the bottom of the Atlantic Division with a 12-14-4 record and 28 points—not much, as they are only 7 points away from a wild card due to the close location in the standings.

The absence of Ellis from the squad puts a lot of pressure on Alex Lyon and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, thus creating a very uncertain situation for a team that has been grappling with finding stability in net.

Colten Ellis' NHL Debut Ends With A Win! | Buffalo Sabres Beat Detroit Red Wings 4-2 | Highlights

Furthermore, Buffalo will have to bear the burden of being the team that has not qualified for the playoffs for the longest period of time in the NHL, having missed the playoffs every year since 2011. Losing Ellis will not end their hopes of qualification, but it will certainly reduce the margin of error during a very critical period of the season.The transfer of Colten Ellis to the injured reserve list comes at a very inconvenient time for the Sabres, who are very much in need of a miracle to stay in the playoffs. Sabres Place Colten Ellis On Injured Reserve
============================================

December 11, 2025 at 4:53 pm CDT | by [Josh Erickson](https://www.prohockeyrumors.com/author/jpepdx) [Leave a Comment](https://www.prohockeyrumors.com/2025/12/sabres-place-colten-ellis-on-injured-reserve.html#respond)

The Sabres placed goaltender **[Colten Ellis](https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/e/ellisco01.html?utm_medium=linker&utm_source=www.prohockeyrumors.com&utm_campaign=2025-12-11_hr)** on injured reserve today, per [Paul Hamilton of WGR Sports Radio 550](https://x.com/pham1717/status/1999176200028086444?s=20). That opens the roster spot for forward **Trevor Kuntar** to join the team after [signing a two-way deal yesterday](https://www.prohockeyrumors.com/2025/12/buffalo-sabres-sign-trevor-kuntar-to-one-year-deal.html).

Ellis, 25, was pulled from Tuesday’s overtime win over the Oilers by concussion spotters late in the first period. He took an inadvertent shoulder to the head from Edmonton right winger **[David Tomasek](https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/t/tomasda01.html?utm_medium=linker&utm_source=www.prohockeyrumors.com&utm_campaign=2025-12-11_hr)** as he was cutting across the crease with the puck ([video via Crossing Swords on X](https://x.com/CrossSwordsPod/status/1998584889298530409?s=20)).

For at least the next two games, Buffalo’s three-goalie rotation is down to two. The Sabres nearly lost another netminder today when **[Alex Lyon](https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/l/lyonal01.html?utm_medium=linker&utm_source=www.prohockeyrumors.com&utm_campaign=2025-12-11_hr)** briefly left practice in apparent pain, but he returned to the session and is expected to start tonight’s game against the Canucks as scheduled, per [Rachel Lenzi of The Buffalo News](https://x.com/rachelmlenzi/status/1999218002663805224?s=20).

Ellis, a 2019 third-round pick by the Blues, didn’t have any NHL experience entering the season. He spent most of his pro career in the ECHL until last year, when he broke out as St. Louis’ third-stringer. He took over the starting role in AHL Springfield with a .922 SV% in 42 appearances.

The Blues were hoping to sneak him through waivers to start the season to keep him as insurance behind their tandem of **[Jordan Binnington](https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/b/binnijo01.html?utm_medium=linker&utm_source=www.prohockeyrumors.com&utm_campaign=2025-12-11_hr)** and **[Joel Hofer](https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/h/hoferjo01.html?utm_medium=linker&utm_source=www.prohockeyrumors.com&utm_campaign=2025-12-11_hr)**. However, the Sabres took their chance to claim him with **[Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen](https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/l/luukkuk01.html?utm_medium=linker&utm_source=www.prohockeyrumors.com&utm_campaign=2025-12-11_hr)** facing injury concerns and the since-released **[Alexandar Georgiev](https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/g/georgal01.html?utm_medium=linker&utm_source=www.prohockeyrumors.com&utm_campaign=2025-12-11_hr)** coming off a disappointing preseason showing.

Instead of placing Ellis on waivers when Luukkonen returned and risk St. Louis reclaiming him, Buffalo has opted to carry three goaltenders for most of the season. With seven starts, Ellis has gotten the least playing time of the trio. He’s had a couple of standout appearances – a .935 SV% in his NHL debut against the Red Wings on Oct. 22 and a 32-save performance against the Oilers last month with just one goal allowed. On the whole, though, he’s been just as middling as what Luukkonen and Lyon have put on offer this season.

Ellis is the only Buffalo goalie with an above-average record, going 4-3-0, but his .895 SV% is second behind Lyon’s .899, and his 3.25 GAA is the worst. His -0.9 goals saved above expected put him in the middle between Lyon’s neutral mark and Luukkonen’s -2.4, per [MoneyPuck](https://moneypuck.com/goalies.htm).

It will be Luukkonen and Lyon’s crease for at least the next couple of games. Ellis will be eligible to come off IR on Dec. 18 against the Flyers.

They’ll use his spot to get the newly signed Kuntar into the mix. The Buffalo native is expected to sit in the press box tonight instead of making his NHL debut, though. The 2020 third-rounder by the Bruins began the season on a minor-league contract with AHL Rochester and had nine goals in 24 games, tied for the team lead, before landing an NHL deal.

[Ellis](https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/players/3140305/ellis/fantasy/) (concussion) was placed on injured reserve Thursday, Rachel Lenzi of The Buffalo News reports.

Ellis landed in the concussion protocol after exiting Tuesday's game against the Oilers, and he'll be sidelined for at least a week while he recovers. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Alex Lyon should see time in the crease while Ellis is unavailable.

Ellis (concussion) will be reevaluated Friday, Bill Hoppe of the Olean Times Herald reports.

Ellis (concussion) was placed on injured reserve Thursday, Rachel Lenzi of The Buffalo News reports.

Scouting Report

Like a lot of goaltenders, he is resilient and has proven his stock at several different stops along the way in his journey to the National Hockey League. Does not have ideal size for a netminder at the highest level but makes up for it with a high hockey IQ and great positioning.

**Long Range Potential:** Depth goaltender with a little upside.
